question: Can a fixed fraction of the L cut-adjacent signed charges, even together with every bulk charge, produce nonvanishing logical-sector contrast as L grows?
scope: Canonical square independent-current channel at fixed edge activity 0<p<1, any edge-wise orientation bias, right rough-boundary parity H, all bulk charges Q_B, and charges Q_T on any subset T of the L cut-adjacent measured vertices. Other strip charges are unobserved. Exact finite-size theorem only; no claim for the complete strip record.

competing_outcomes.parity_mask: Cut activities at rows outside T remain independent Bernoulli(p), multiply every conditional sector polarization by (1-2p)^(L-|T|), and force the partial-record Bayes risk near one half when the number omitted grows.
competing_outcomes.leakage: Some supposedly unobserved cut activity enters Q_B or Q_T, invalidating the factorization.

method: Prove disjoint-edge conditional factorization, then audit canonical cut endpoints at existing L=3,5,7,11 and check all eight L=3 strip subsets at each retained q=0.5,0.9,1 against exact sector masses. No new physical samples, sizes, noise points, or bootstrap.
acceptance: For every exact control, partial-record contrast is at most |1-2p|^(L-|T|) within 1e-12; all cut endpoints satisfy the required disjointness; record the all-size Bayes-risk lower bound and the limit for L-|T| tending to infinity.
stop_rule: Fail closed on any incidence or exact-mass violation. Never infer the full-record phase at p=.30 or a threshold from this partial-record theorem.
literature_basis: The independent ternary edge prior and physically measured signed charges are the registered Lab 006/007 model; this is a model-specific parity-factorization corollary rather than a literature-derived transition claim.
